Meanwhile, Yuki's friend Masami is thrilled with the flash mob surprise her boyfriend Tomo organized for her birthday. Feeling envious, Yuki decides to confide in Kento, but...

>> Story 2: "Hashiru Toriteki" (走る取的)
Middle-aged salaryman Shinoda and his coworker Kamei are joking and teasing someone they know at a pub. A toriteki (low-ranking sumo wrestler) mistakes their conversation as being about him and follows them outside. Shinoda and Kamei, feeling scared, try to escape the wrestler but...

--- Adapted from the novel "Hashiru Toriteki" (走る取的) by Tsutsui Yasutaka (筒井康隆).

>> Story 3: "Mirai Dorobo" (未来ドロボウ)
University student Shirai Naoki struggles to find employment and is dissatisfied with his daily routine. Meanwhile, successful cerebrophysiologist Oba Kunimasa, who is wealthy but unwell, envies Shirai's youth. One day, when they wake up...

>> Story 4: "Hieru" (冷える)
Yoriko Shikura, a part-time supermarket cashier and housewife, feels unappreciated by her manager, coworkers, husband, and children. One day, she's forced to work overtime, taking inventory of frozen food in a large refrigerator.

>> Story 5: "Fanamo" (ファナモ)
Atsuko is contemplating marriage with her boyfriend, Takuya, but her father opposes it because Takuya has converted to "fanamo," a scentless, inorganic black stick considered the next generation of excrement. Despite Takuya's persuasion for Atsuko to switch to "fanamo," she remains hesitant.

synopsis:
There is a small old-fashioned shop called ‘Fuji Family’ at the foot of Mt Fuji that is a convenience store in name only. It is run by three sisters who are known for their beauty. Dependable Oguni Takako is the eldest sister, free-spirited Nasumi, the second sister, is the complete opposite of Takako in both personality and lifestyle, and tactful Tsukimi is the youngest sister. Although Nasumi lived and got married in Tokyo, she abruptly came back with her husband Kinoshita Hideo, but died suddenly of illness eight years ago. 

Takako finally wed Haruta Masao, with whom she has had an enduring but difficult relationship, this year. The newlyweds now live in an apartment nearby but Takako constantly comes to ‘Fuji Family’. Hideo had a shotgun marriage with Aiko but he still lives with the Ogunis and runs the shop. A new part-timer Purio, whose actual name is Kuromatsu Heizo, has joined ‘Fuji Family’. And Nasumi appears as a ghost to grandaunt Shoko who is the only one who can see her. 

One day towards the end of the year, Takako sees a magazine article about the famous soothsayer Kitty Toyama and realises that she was her junior high school classmate. Kitty had made an outrageous prediction concerning Takako’s fate in her junior high school diary. With the addition of a new ghost Tesshin and Shoko’s friend Tokuzo, disturbance erupts in the lives of every member of the family.

synopsis:
Set in Kumamoto, one year after Iruma Michio was transferred out of “Ichikei”. Whilst Michio is busy vigorously conducting trials at the Kumamoto District Court 2nd Branch, a case of grievous bodily harm arises, revolving around a young man named Suwa Haruto who intervened in a gang fight and is in critical condition. The suspect, Uchida Wataru, pleads guilty to the charges, and on the surface, it appears to be a cut and dry case that will result in a suspended sentence. synopsis: After the war, the Occupation Forces’ General Headquarters was about to seize the broadcasting station, NHK, with the objective of directing its broadcasts in September 1945 (Showa 20). Takeshita Mitsue, an announcer whom Shindo is familiar with, is forced out of work in his presence due to the demobilisation and return of male staff members. The censors of the General Headquarters are meticulous, and in particular, George Mabuchi, an American interpreter of Japanese descent, has an overbearing manner of speech that grates on their nerves for someone who looks Japanese. Although Shindo appears to give into despair, he is cheered up by the positivity of Mitsue who has been returned to do odd jobs because of her family’s circumstances. Meanwhile, Shindo and the others get instructions from the General Headquarters to think of a new music programme. Influenced by Mitsue and the people around him, Shindo writes up a proposal for the “Red & White Music Contest”. However, he receives complaints from the General Headquarters and that kills his enthusiasm. They say that the Japanese characters for “contest” in the programme name “Red & White Music Contest” will encourage war. Shindo engages in a battle of words with the General Headquarters, and manages to gain consent to call it “Music Contest”. But he is warned by Mabuchi to stick entirely to the script. On the other hand, record companies vehemently protest the attempt to pit singers against each other. Furthermore, Namiki Michiko of Ringo no Uta fame, the programme’s main attraction, turns down an appearance. She is not able to sing because she lost her family in the war. They eventually succeed in persuading her through Shindo’s fervour and Mitsue’s wit. The day of broadcast arrives. synopsis:
This feature drama, produced to celebrate the 60th anniversary of Fuji TV, is an adaptation of Victor Hugo's classic masterpiece Les Miserables set in the 1990s in Japan.
 In Kobe in 1993, Jun Baba gets taken to a juvenile prison due to a killing of a man who cheated his mother out of all her money in self-defense. One day, he hears that his younger brother, who has been desperately ill, is in a critical condition and breaks out. However, he finds out his brother is already dead. In the depth of despair, he tries to kill himself but is saved by a man who runs a self-support facility. He begins to live at the place, and befriends with Takumi Watanabe aspiring to be a lawyer. In 1995, the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake hits and their friendship comes to an end. Crushed under the debris, Takumi persuades Jun to live his life instead. Jun swears to live on assuming Takumi's identity.
 Meanwhile, Ryosuke Saito, the son of the man that Jun has killed, finds his life turns dramatically.
 Bound together by fate, the two meet in Tokyo in 2004, as a lawyer and a police detective. Getting along with each other, Ryosuke finds out that Takumi is actually Jun, his father's murderer. Ryosuke tries but fails to catch Jun, and the story follows Jun living a hidden life in the countryside of Fukushima in 2019.
 The long journey of the two men, as a fugitive and a pursuer, is about to end here.
 With atonement and forgiveness as its themes, this story illuminates the lives of some seventeen people, focusing on the two men who lived through these turbulent 30 years.

synopsis:
Members of the 13th Section of the Kyoto Police Investigation Division 1 such as Kiyoko Tokiya (Kazuki Sawamura) and Tomoka Saai (Miori Enomoto) depart for an annual comfort trip. This year, it was a mystery tour, and it was a hotel near the top of Mt.
However, despite being a large inn, there are only 13 guests and a group of 6 guests. Moreover, these six people are somewhere else strange. When they felt lonely, when they asked them about the situation, they revealed that they had just met. They are acquaintances of female university student Kuroe Michiru who died 7 years ago, psychiatrist Kazumi Sone (Daisuke Daito), model Mai Akashi (ononoka), and event company executive Anzai Features such as Kiki (Kazuki Namioka), freelance writer Ikuo Miyaura (Asaharu Hasegawa), cram school teacher Toko Kasagi (Mao Miyachi), and flower shop manager Shigekazu Makimura (Toshiyuki Nagashima) are all different. They all came in after receiving a mysterious invitation to the hotel.　
In fact, seven years ago, an IT company president who stayed at this hotel was killed in a nearby forest. The next day, a fire went up from the coffin hut behind the hotel, and Michiru's body was found in the burnt-out ruins. Initially, both were thought to be the work of robbery murderers who were running away, but the victim's president's wife turned out to be a true criminal. The wife not only killed her husband for the purpose of property, but also accidentally thought that Michiru who stayed at the same hotel had caught a lie alibi and ended up killing.
The next morning, the 13-person group leaves the hotel and heads for the hot spring. When she was told that she had lost her memory without Sagami, she also stayed in the inn. However, immediately after that, someone broke the one-way tunnel leading from the hotel to the city, making it impossible to pass! The antenna and telephone line were also cut off, making it impossible to use communication means. In other words, Tokiya, Sasei, and 6 guests were trapped in a building that became a “land solitary island” where I could not go down the mountain or ask for help!
Immediately after, a corpse of Mai who was hung on a nearby tourist spot "Eternal Love Bell" was found, and everyone was astonished! After that, a murder happened in the closed hotel premises ...!? Eventually, Toshiya himself was in danger, and that led to the return of 20 years of lost memory! ? (toei.co.jp)

However, she is not able to broach the topic to Takeshi. The job she has finally secured does not work out as she thought too. While she sulks in disgruntlement for successive days, her mother Fumiko comes to Tokyo from their hometown. Suzu’s pregnancy is exposed and she is berated. synopsis:
On a train bound for the snowy mountains of northwestern Japan, a writer named Shimamura notices two fellow-passengers: an ill man named Yukio and the young woman who attends him, Yoko. Gazing at their otherworldly reflection in the train window, Shimamura wonders if they might be husband and wife.

Arriving at an inn, Shimamura spends the night with a geisha named Komako. The next day, he visits the room where Komako lives and finds Yoko there. It seems that Komako and Yoko live in the same house as the ill man Yukio. Komako explains that she has known Yukio since they were children, and Shimamura also comes to understand that Komako became a geisha in order to help pay Yukio's medical bills.

But if so, why is Yoko the one who nurses Yukio? The complex relations among Komako, Yukio and Yoko gradually become clear to him, though he views them and his own involvement as "wasted effort."

synopsis:
"Power Office Girls" revolves around the office ladies (OL) of General Affairs department 2 (Shomu ni, or GA-2) in a large multinational company called Manpan Corporation.

GA-2 is called "the graveyard for female office ladies", simply because it is the place where female employees are dumped should they mess up big time elsewhere. Rarely anyone is ever allowed to leave for other more purposeful departments. Jobs include replacing used toilet rolls, changing light-bulbs, organizing company outings among other menial stuff. As an added incentive, their department is located in the nether regions of the company - in the basement, and is in fact a disused store room.

synopsis: The treasure of the company Teikoku Shinju, a natural pearl called the ‘Golden Star’ is stolen. The ‘Golden Star’ is said to be expensive enough to buy a New York skyscraper. The theft is made public and Teikoku Shinju’s share price plunges. This incident triggers an internal struggle between the company’s chairman Iwakura Jusaburo (Nishida Toshiyuki) and president Iwakura Tsuneko (Zaizen Naomi) for the company president’s position. Tsuneko, the daughter of Teikoku Shinju’s founder and Jusaburo’s stepsister, is forced to take responsibility and step down. Learning about the fmaily’s infighting from media reports, Sawaguchi Nobuko (Yonekura Ryoko) hides her beauty with black glasses and loose, disheveled hair, and goes into the home as a housekeeper. She has a specific objective to fulfil at the Iwakura household. Nobuko had gone to see the ‘Golden Star’, which was displayed in a department store, and encountered an enigmatic man (Yokota Eiji) who suddenly appeared in front of her. The man seemed to have a connection to the ‘Golden Pearl’ and the Iwakura family. He had encouraged her to try wearing the pearl like the ‘Girl with a Pearl Earring’ painted by Vemeer. As customers and news reporters swarmed around them, Nobuko had fled the place without thinking. But in doing so, the precious pearl earring was lost. According to store personnel, that man had taken it out. Nobuko’s intuition tells her that the man is involved in the theft of the ‘Golden Star’ and she guesses he will show up at the Iwakura home some day. There is a portrait in the Iwakura home of a man who resembles him as if in confirmation of her conjecture. What is this man’s true identity? After that, the more the battle between the chairman and company president heats up, the more the share price of Teikoku Shinju continues to mysteriously rise. Why did the pearl disappear? Nobuko who has peeked at the secrets and conspiracies in the mansion, takes action.

synopsis:
Three stories from the Shiratsuna Island:

**Mikan no Hana
Shiratsuna Island, Japan's last island city, is merging with a city across the shore. Tomita Misato, a housewife on the island, despises her older sister, novelist Katsuragi Shoko, who left 20 years ago. Shoko returns for a ceremony, sparking old resentments. Misato's memories resurface, linking to a past summer with a young man named Kenichi. Shoko reveals a surprising truth about their family. **Umi no Hoshi
Hamasaki Yohei, a Shiratsuna Island native, resides on the outskirts of Tokyo with his wife Tomomi and son Taichi. One day, a postcard from his high school classmate, Mano Misaki, arrives. She's coming to Tokyo to discuss Yohei's father, Hideo, who vanished suddenly 20 years ago. Yohei's mother, Yoshiko, tirelessly searched for Hideo. Yohei, as a young boy, even tried to help by fishing. Mano Kosaku, a fisherman, once aided him. Misaki, Kosaku's daughter, wants to share a secret her father recently disclosed.

**Kumo no Ito
Renowned artist Kurosaki Hirotaka, a Shiratsuna Island native, returns home after seven years but falls into a coma after a mysterious accident at sea. Media speculations about foul play surface, and Hirotaka harbors a dark past from his childhood marked by bullying due to an incident caused by his mother, Ritsuko. A month earlier, he reluctantly agreed to attend the 50th-anniversary party of Matoba Iron Works, organized by his pushy ex-classmate, Matoba Yuya. Hirotaka's discomfort grows, leaving the question of what transpired.

He comes back to Japan after five years although there is the risk of a relapse and starts work at Kera General Hospital. But the pediatric doctors including Miyoshi Masayasu are worn out because of the exhausting work and many lawsuits. Saijo worries about the doctor Oda Reiko who extremely detests risks and handles her duties mechanically. Reiko was transferred to the pediatric department from the department of surgery as a result of some incident three years ago. One day, Saijo notices that a baby girl diagnosed with asthma is acting strangely. He discovers a tumour from the results of a medical examination. Furthermore, this is not a mere tumour. synopsis:
At the venerable Fukumaru Department Store in Kobe, Samejima Shizuo, who worked her way up from a part-timer, has been through a lot and built a career at the western confectionery department. She became a full-fledged employee following the success of a renewal plan of the store, which she handled besides western confectionery. However, she is assigned to the all-male external sales department as the only female in a sudden personnel transfer and also because it is the intention of the managing director, Benikura Eiichi. In truth, various members are being assembled so that the store can link up with the customers of the well-connected, charismatic Hatori Shiro, in preparation for his retirement. Shizuo’s husband, Kanno Hisaomi, who works for the same department store group and currently lives in Tokyo, understands her role. Shizuo has been successful in her work all this while. Although she is disconcerted and out of her element in the world of external sales, she goes to customer places with the aim of completing deals. An external sales staff takes care of customers every need – from jewellery, cosmetics, wedding favours to home improvements. It is a completely different world from the customers Shizuo has played host to so far. Furthermore, these “upper class” people who appear snobbish on the surface, have families, setbacks, sorrow, glamour and dreams too. Shizuo pushes ahead with the network of contacts that she had cultivated at the western confectionery department and store development section as well as her own self-motivation. There are two persons who give her a hard time at every turn. Ochi Takashi, her superior and the section head of the department, and Masuya Shuhei, her slightly “flawed” junior and rival. Masuya, who comes from a wealthy Nara family, joined the department store after graduating from a famous private university. He is, in a sense, an elite. Even after his transfer to the external sales department, he fully uses his family connections and meets his quota without effort. Shizuo ends up finding out his secret on the way back from a friend’s wedding ceremony. She struggles with her quota and demanding customer requests every day. There are all sorts of customers like the graceful, gentle wife of a distinguished man from an old samurai family, Kurahashi Kazuko; the nagging wife of a hospital director, Tsuru Akiko; a trouble making customer, Shimada Goro; and a Thai businessman. In the midst of this, Shizuo secures Mitani Juri, who has moved from Tokyo, as a new customer. However, she causes some trouble for Juri. While Shizuo is in despair, she hears news of the sudden death of her Thai businessman customer. He has left word of an outrageous wish for his funeral arrangements.

~~ Adapted from the 2013 novel "Jouryuu Kaikyuu Fukumaru Hyakkaten Gaishoubu" by Takadono Madoka.

synopsis:
One day, Tomonaga Takashi, a medical representative of pharmaceutical company Tenei Seiyaku, is suddenly suspected of molesting inside a train by male and female strangers. He has an important appointment and tries to get away. However, Nitta Masato, who rushed over from the police box in front of the train station where he had been on duty, arrests Tomonaga as he fights back. This is Nitta’s first achievement as a new police officer. 

Tomonaga is taken to the police precinct where he insists on his innocence the whole time. But no one listens to him. The case is sent to the prosecutors and he is charged despite denying the allegation. On a later date, Nitta sees the female university student who was molested, together with the male eyewitness at a bar. The two of them seem to have been acquainted more than six months ago. Nitta begins to have misgivings about whether she was really molested. He is admonished by a senior police officer who tells him that the court will decide if Tomonaga is guilty or innocent but he cannot let go of his suspicion. So he seeks the help of a wily lawyer Gomi Jinsuke whom the police treat like an enemy, and starts to get to the bottom of the matter. Who framed Tomonaga? And what was the objective? The three men are dragged into the darkness of a case deeper than they expected and this will force Niita to choose whether to continue being a police officer...

synopsis: Aku Yu  was a songwriter who put out more than 500 songs in his lifetime. His songs spanned a wide genre from idol songs, enka, folk songs to songs for anime and commercials. He was called a hit maker for the many famous songs he composed which added colour to the period. These songs continue to be appreciated even to this day. Aku’s wife Yuko  sees female high school students humming to her husband’s songs and recalls the time when she met him… In 1963, Aku, then known as Fukada Hiroyuki, was a salaryman who worked for an advertising agency. That was where he met Yuko. The two of them were similar in character and started dating. They got married a year later. After that, he began working part-time as a broadcast writer without the knowledge of his company and came to use the pen name “Aku Yu”. He eventually resigned from the advertising agency and became a freelance broadcaster because he wanted to write something. He even took on the challenge of writing song lyrics and displayed his talent, making Moriyama Kayoko’s Shiroi Chou No Samba a huge hit. Wanting to produce popular songs which would create an era, Aku made the decision to write songs seriously. He got increasingly busy with work such that he came back home to Yuko and their son Taro once in every two or three months. Then in 1971, Nippon TV producer Ikezawa Fumio called Aku to participate in the launch of a new programme. Ikezawa wished to create a star from the TV station and had the intention of producing a new audition programme. Aku’s ideas were sought and he proposed an unconventional programme format where the entire audition process would be broadcast and open to scrutiny. This was the beginning of the legendary audition programme Star Tanjou! It was decided that they would serve as the judges and Star Tanjou! finally premiered. However, the star contestants whom Aku, Ikezawa and the production crew had anticipated, did not materialise and the programme got off to a rocky start.

synopsis:
One morning in mid-summer, a dead man with a knife in his chest is discovered on a park bench. The victim is Shinojima Taku, the vocalist of a famous rock band who had made waves after winning a literary prize for his first novel. At the meeting of the investigation task force, Director Tsurusaki gets excited to have the murder case of a well-known person. Because Shinojima’s award-winning novel was poorly-received, this gave rise to rumours that his win was rigged, and he had received considerable criticism from book critics as well as the general public. 

While the attention is focused on Shinojima’s interpersonal relationships, the Tokyo Metropolitan Department’s detective with the best arrest rate, Inukai Hayato, finds it odd that there was barely blood spurted from the dead man although he was stabbed to death. The investigators hurriedly begin the investigation. At the same time, a man comes to the police precinct where the investigation task force is based to turn himself in for the murder. Calling himself a novelist, Arashiuma Shuto confesses that he killed Shinojima out of hate. However, Inukai and Kotegawa Kazuya do not believe his clumsy words during the interrogation. 

Meanwhile, Toyosaki Sayaka, Inukai’s only daughter with his ex-wife, is discharged from the hospital after a successful kidney transplant surgery three months ago. She makes the acquaintance of a popular top idol, Shikura Kaede, at a symposium that she began to attend by chance. Sayaka has few friends because of her long hospitalisation. Her friendship with Kaede deepens, and she learns that Kaede belongs to the same entertainment agency as Shinojima. Inukai and Kotegawa continue investigating by questioning Shinojima’s wife, entertainment agency company president Takamori Hideo, and Vivre & Co, the publishing company that organised the literary prize. 

Then, a letter claiming responsibility for the kidnapping of Shikura Kaede is delivered to Kanto Chuo TV. A photograph of Kaede bound in packing tape and her mobile phone are enclosed with the letter. The criminal demands that hostage negotiations be done through a news programme televised nationwide and designates Inukai to be the negotiator. What is the criminal’s true intention?

synopsis: Called the “magnet man”, Oba Sousuke (Mukai Osamu) possesses a superhuman ability to see through people’s lifestyles, personalities, upbringing as well as jobs at a glance, and find perfect matches. Females gather at the farm he runs at the foot of Yatsugatake in Nagano Prefecture every day, yearning to get married. But he would cut them down with the words, “You’re a disappointment”. On the other hand, in Tokyo, Kohinata Shion (Aibu Saki), who heads the Matchmaking Department at an event company which Himuro Kotaro (Kaname Jun) runs, clashes with Sousuke, but changes her mind about a marriage with conditions because of his words. “Magnet man” matchmaking events labelled “Magnet Man Coupling” are supposed to continue at the event company, but Sousuke’s priority is farming so he cancels at the last minute. Naturally, their reputation hits rock bottom. Shion is at the end of her rope, and the Matchmaking Department ends up becoming a complete burden. Even Kitajima Ayumi (Matsuoka Mayu), a young staff of the Accounting Department, makes sarcastic remarks about her. One day, a young man Saeko Wataru (Kiriyama Ren) is headhunted by Himuro to save the Matchmaking Department from its plight by tapping on the knowledge from the successes he achieved in dating social networking services in America. Ayumi swiftly latches onto Wataru who is her “Mr Right”. Meanwhile, Shion is overwhelmed by Wataru’s frequent physical contact and flattery. Wataru, who has a keen business sense, takes a great interest in the Magnet Man. He quickly proposes creating a vegetable restaurant where matchmaking events can also be held and succeeds in calling Sousuke to Tokyo. An awkward Sousuke who has been taught by childhood friend Shindo (Aoyagi Sho) to neither say “like” nor to kiss, slams his hand on the wall in front of Shion and she wonders, “Are we a couple?” The two of them who are in a delicate relationship, start living together in her apartment when Sousuke comes to Tokyo prepare for the store opening. Then Shion’s grandmother Yuri (Baisho Mitsuko) moves in with her and she begins to meddle in everything by trying to play their matchmaker. Meanwhile, a very complicated woman appears. Although she is popular on first impression, she does not last with anyone. The 38-year-old career woman, Oshima Mariko (Ryo), participates in Shion’s matchmaking event, but complains about not being a couple with someone. She is actually a famous person who joins numerous dating agencies and matchmaking parties in order to meet the person of her destiny, and makes complaints about the organiser once things do not go well. Sousuke cuts a haughty Mariko down with the words, “You’re a disappointment.” In fact, he even identifies the reason why Mariko ended up becoming such a “heavy woman”. Will Sousuke and Shion untangle the idiosyncratic Mariko’s complications and be able to lead her to happiness?

Referred to as the Pearl of the Orient, supermodel Miori Reiko has had her fair share of scandals due to her eccentricity and her wild love affairs. One day, Reiko is found dead in her apartment by her housekeeper, Ota Michiko. The medical examiner found traces of potassium cyanide in her body, which kick-started a major police investigation into her death. 

The main suspect is Sasahara Nobuo, a doctor at one of the major hospitals, who happens to be Reiko's ex-fiancé. Sasahara had left his wife and kids to be with Reiko, forsaking his reputation and social status, only to have the engagement end within 3 months' time. The broken engagement made all the news, with the reporters all labelling Sasahara as a weak, pathetic middle-aged man who was played out by Reiko. 

When the police found Sasahara's fingerprints on the broken glass in Reiko's bedroom and his leftover cigarette stub in her ashtray, together with evidence of him withdrawing potassium cyanide from his workplace, they were all ready to charge him with the murder of Reiko. Except, Sasahara vehemently denies killing her.

On the other hand, Sawamori Eijiro, the CEO of the apparel company that Reiko is the spokesperson for, had committed suicide and left a note confessing to her murder. As their company's image girl, Reiko had helped to successfully launch their brand of clothing. In his note, Sawamori claimed to have threatened Reiko and was, in fact, seen by an eyewitness to be at her apartment on the night of her murder.

titles.native: 眩 北斎の娘
akas: Kurara: The Dazzling Life of Hokusai's Daughter

synopsis:
Oei, later known as Katsushika Oi, was born the third daughter of Edo’s talented painter Katsushika Hokusai and his second wife Koto. Although Oei became the wife of a town painter for a time, her love of the paintbrush more than her husband spelt disaster and she comes back home to Hokusai from the family she had married into. This is how Oei starts to help her father out in his painting of the “insurmountable high wall”. 
Meanwhile, Oei can only talk to the painter Ikeda Zenjiro, who is her father’s student, about her pain and worries. Zenjiro has taken Edo by storm as Keisai Eisen, the master of ukiyo-e portraying beautiful women. He visits regularly because he admires Hokusai and secretly likes Oei although their relationship is like childhood friends. Oei respects her father whose paintings fascinated her and continues to work as a painter who supports him behind the scenes. When Hokusai’s masterpiece Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji was completed, she was also by his side. 
As Hokusai progressed in age, he could no longer move the paintbrush as he wished but Oei continued to draw his paintings as her father’s “shadow”. She was content to be the shadow while he dazzled. And she kept on painting, obsessed with colour and shadow. Time eventually passes and by the time Oei has developed her own unique style, Zenjiro whom she had constantly turned to for support and even Hokusai have left this world. Now over 60 years old, Oei arrives at a single truth, “The shadow shapes everything. The light illuminates it. This world is made of light and shadow.”

synopsis:
An omnibus special comprised of five segments:

>> Story 1: "Nabebuta" (鍋蓋)
One day, Furukawa Naomi receives a recommendation on her smartphone for a product favored by her senior, Atsushi Arai. She starts buying recommended items and becomes grateful to her surroundings, including Arai. However, one night she sees Arai walking with her colleague Teshima Yuka, leading to confusion in their relationship.

>> Story 2: "Koi no Kioku, Tomaranai De" (恋の記憶、止まらないで)
Singer-songwriter Murase Shiho struggles with writer's block and harsh comments on social media, causing disappointment from her husband Nakai Kenji. One day, she recalls a melody from a childhood commercial and decides to use it for a new song, receiving positive feedback. However, she is shocked to discover that the melody is from her past and was used in a childhood program she appeared in.

>> Story 3: "Cold Sleep" (コールドスリープ)
Fujita Goro, hailed as a visionary in the IT world, dreams of space travel and enters cold sleep in hopes of a cure for his terminal illness.

>> Story 4: "Solo Camp" (ソロキャンプ)
Fujiwara Taketo finds solace in solo camping after completing a big job. During one of his outings, a sharply dressed man interrupts, discussing his daughter before ominously asking about Fujiwara's solo camping experience. When Fujiwara expresses his joy in solitude, the man unexpectedly brandishes a knife.

>> Story 5: "Emiron" (恵美論)
Emi Yoshimura falls asleep in class and wakes up to find her name and life story integrated into the curriculum, with textbooks now based on "Emi theory." Her embarrassment grows as lessons focus on her body and romance. Later, she meets Ryosuke Izawa, who confesses his affection for "Emi."

synopsis:
An omnibus special comprised of four segments:

>> Story 1: "Ato 15 Byo de Shinu" (あと15秒で死ぬ)
Pharmacist Mikami Megumi, working late, finds herself frozen in time with a bullet suspended in front of her. A god of death reveals she's been shot in the back, but she still has 15 seconds of life left, during which time can be stopped or moved. The identity of the shooter and motive remain unknown. Megumi must act quickly in her final moments.

>> Story 2: "Sanzunokawa Outlet Park" (三途の川アウトレットパーク)
Kimura Takashi wakes up near the Sanzu River, a place where he can earn "virtue" based on his past deeds. He meets Tanaka Haru, who wants to improve at baseball in his next life. Takashi, troubled by his poor eyesight, wishes for better eyes in his next life. He recalls Mei, a patient he cared for, who admired his eyes but died young. Takashi wonders about Mei's fate and a sprout appears. What will happen to them?

>> Story 3: "Deja Vu" (デジャヴ)
Hikari experiences repeated déjà vu moments on her birthday, including encounters with a mysterious masked man. Later, she finds herself in a pitch-black room with her father, Masataka, a brain scientist, and his colleague, Shindo Aki. The connection between Hikari's déjà vu and Masataka's research is revealed as they confront the identity of the masked man.

>> Story 4: "Naru" (成る)
Famous Go player Iwaya Kentaro faces an AI opponent named "Nuisance" that triggers traumatic memories with its moves. The game forces Iwaya to confront past scandals and personal traumas. Despite his emotional turmoil, memories of his mother's support inspire him to fight back. Can Iwaya overcome the AI and regain control of the game?

titles.native: 李香蘭

synopsis:
The drama tells the story of Yamaguchi Yoshiko, a Japanese woman born and raised in China during the Japanese occupation of Manchuria. She debuts as the Chinese singer and actress Li Xianglan (Ri Kouran in Japanese), in the hopes that her efforts will work towards the benefit of both Japan and China. Hiding her true nationality, however, she slowly discovers herself becoming a puppet of the Japanese military's propaganda efforts in Manchuria, starring in "national policy" films that humiliate the Chinese people. But billed as the "star of Greater East Asia," her popularity soars across borders to Japan, where she holds a concert that draws thousands to the Nihon Gekijou Theatre and leads to a riot that injures several people. Based on her autobiography, this is the story of her personal struggle amidst military strife between her two homelands. 

Source: Dramawiki

synopsis:
Catherine Turner is the daughter of the Vice President of the United States, and she had come with her father on his official visit to Japan. Since she runs a flower arrangement business back in the US, Catherine decides to stay in Japan to learn Ikebana after her father has returned home at the end of the official visit. Japan's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hamaguchi Yukio, asks his nephew, Ichiro, to escort Catherine during her extended stay in Japan with the strict instructions that he is not to fall in love with her.

Catherine actually started her flower arrangement business after a chance meeting with a Japanese woman, Ogawa Maiko, who had held an exhibition in the United States. She befriended Maiko and is now hoping to reunite with her old friend in Japan. Unable to reach Maiko, Catherine is shocked to learn that Maiko is a victim of a homicide. Thus, with the help of Ichiro, Catherine begins to look into her friend's death.

synopsis:
Housewife Kanako leads an unfulfilling, hurried life in Tokyo. One day, Sakiko, who had been a close friend, suddenly calls her and insists that she come to Itoshima in Fukuoka Prefecture for a class reunion. It has been 35 years since Kanako spent a year there during fourth grade. The place holds many memories for her. She transferred to Itoshima from Tokyo and immediately made friends with Sakiko. They were always together and forgot time as they played around the forest and sea. 
Reliving Itoshima’s environment reminds Kanako of the sparkling feeling she experienced every day at that time. She also unexpectedly recalls the old lady Oharu-san who lived alone deep in the forest and seemed to be the personification of nature. Cats and children were free to come in and out of Oharu-san’s house and she had been interacting with prisoners on death row without being noticed. Kanako remembers posing all sorts of questions like what she thinks about prisoners on death row and what happens to people who die as well as the life lessons Oharu-san taught in the mysterious forest. 
In the middle of this peaceful time, Sakiko tells Kanako the real reason why she called her to Itoshima. This unforeseen confession leaves Kanako lost for words. In addition, she is told about Oharu-san’s sudden disappearance from the village after she transferred to the school. Cruel rumours about suicide had flown about but what is the truth? 
Kanako follows the tracks of Oharu-san who had faced life and death and tries to find their own living clues. Oharu-san’s hidden past and the message that she left to them are revealed.

~~ Adapted from the novel "Ito no Mori no Ie" by Higashi Naoko.

synopsis:
An omnibus special comprised of four segments:

>> Story 1: "City Lives"
Sato Shori and Mizutani Kentaro, the program's making cameraman, were waiting in their car after hearing that they were filming for an animal program, but suddenly they read people's memories and disguise themselves as a city, only to be swallowed up by the world's largest creature, the "town". In order to feature the ecology of a "town" shrouded in mystery, they conducting an in-depth interview with Tsuji Misaki, a conservation officer at the Urban Biological Conservation Organization, who is the only living human in the town. As the investigation progresses, he witnesses mysterious phenomena occurring in the city, such as buildings moving in the wilderness, and buildings growing out of parts of themselves that create "pseudo residents" that look exactly like real humans.

>> Story 2: "Ah, Sokoku yo" (ああ祖国よ)
When a man was working as a program producer for a television station, his superior told him that the Republic of Pagisia, a small country in Africa that had recently become independent, had suddenly declared war on his country, and that two small ships were attacking his country. With 40 days left until he arrive on the mainland, he begin researching the Republic of Pagisia.
~~ Adapted from the story within the novel "Omisore Shakai" (おみそれ社会) by Hoshi Shinichi (星新一 ).

>> Story 3: "Dai 1-kai Tanaka-ke Chichioya Audition" (第1回田中家父親オーディション)
One day, Tanaka Kenichi, an office worker who works overtime every day, is told by his wife Azusa that she has an important report. He thought it was going to be about divorce, but it turned out that they were going to hold an audition to become the father of the Tanaka family, called the "First Tanaka Family Father Audition". This news quickly spread around the world, and Kenichi decided to take on an audition to compete against the unique members to become the father of the Tanaka family.

>> Story 4: "Free" (フリー)
Shinozaki Rika, who works for a video production company, chose an old man who used free material to edit a video for a men's beauty salon. When Rika temporarily stopped her work and came back from a break, she thought that the figure of the "uncle" from the free material that was supposed to be on the computer screen had disappeared, but when she looked back, the "uncle" that was supposed to be on the screen was gone. He had come out into the real world.

synopsis:
Kasahara Sachiko’s parents died young and she lives in a Tokyo apartment with her only sister Nobuko, a journalist for a newspaper’s cultural department. She has not found a job and has been interviewing at a number of companies. On this day, Sachiko bids farewell to Nobuko who is leaving for a holiday at Lake Towada in Tohoku, and sets off for another company interview. 

This should have been the usual scene of the two sisters who share a close relationship. But that night, Sachiko gets news that Nobuko was killed in an accident, and for some reason, Nobuko lost her life in Nagano which is a different place from what she had told her. Nobuko’s colleague and fellow journalist Yoshii Ryoichi suddenly shows up before a grieving Sachiko. He sets out to investigate the mystery of Nobuko’s death together with Sachiko, but she does not know his true intentions. 
Meanwhile, Sachiko starts to work at the newspaper as her sister’s replacement and goes to meet the cultural figures that Nobuko had been in charge of when she was alive. Among these people with habits which are unimaginable from their glamorous appearances, is the pediatrician Nishiwaki Mitsutaro who writes a column for the newspaper. He seems to be the greatest philanderer in celebrity circles even though he has a wif, and calls Sachiko out many times. 
But right after that, Machida Tomoe, who had been her sister’s colleague in the same department, commits suicide. She leaves behind cryptic words for Sachiko regarding Nobuko’s death. “There is someone who should take responsibility”, “All the more if it is a famous person”. Sachiko’s hunch is that her sister’s death is connected to someone prominent that she had been dating while alive. 

However, the more she attempts to learn the truth, the more “suspects” meet suspicious deaths one after another until she no longer knows who is her friend or foe. Sachiko has unwittingly been sucked into a deep darkness as if she is wandering about in a dark, dense sea of trees with no exit.

synopsis:
An omnibus special comprised of four segments:

>> Story 1: "Follower" (フォロワー)
Fujita Koharu, known as the sparkly Minato-ku OL_Haru, lives a glamorous but fake life on social media to gain followers. In reality, she works for a printing company and lives modestly. Koharu's joy comes from increasing her follower count, especially the support from Mimiko@Remote Countryside. When she loses a survey to Uruwashi no Uketsukejou Sayu, who has fewer followers, Koharu's fighting spirit is ignited. However, she receives a message from Mimiko revealing that her real life is being watched nearby.

>> Story 2: "Furin Keisatsu" (不倫警察)
Kuzuki Yoshio, a peaceful salaryman, witnesses his subordinate being arrested for adultery, part of a government crackdown on affairs due to public pressure. Adultery is severely punished, and novels, dramas, and movies about affairs are banned. One day, Yoshio accidentally sends a lovey-dovey emoji to his subordinate Kyono Suzuka, leading to his own arrest by adultery control officers.

>> Story 3: "Ashita e no Warp" (明日へのワープ)
Kobayashi Mineo, an aspiring movie director, struggles as his peers find success in careers and start families. Frustrated and exhausted, he seeks help from psychiatrist Udo Kimiyasu, who prescribes a mysterious drug called Airium. Airium erases his memories of the next 24 hours, offering a chance to escape awful incidents. Mineo hopes this drug will give him control over his life, but faces unforeseen consequences.

>> Story 4: "Shonen" (少年)
Office lady Okabayashi Haruka witnesses a traffic accident involving a youth named Tayama Keisuke, who later claims his name is Ryota. Haruka is puzzled when she learns that Keisuke is supposedly dead. Meanwhile, she starts receiving silent phone calls at home. Later, she encounters the youth multiple times, and he even helps her with shopping. However, Haruka becomes wary when he starts inspecting her personal belongings.

synopsis:
Misaki Yosuke is a public prosecutor who passed the bar exam with outstanding results and had a promising future. But one day, he suddenly resigns from his job and sets out to become a pianist. Misaki knocks on the door of a mansion built on quiet, high ground in Kamakura to get lodgings. It is the residence of a prominent local figure and multi-millionaire Katsuki Gentaro, who lives with his housekeeper Tsuzuki Michiko. Although Misaki has the temperament of an artist and his eccentricity is hard to handle, Katsuki quickly recognises Misaki’s talent and personality and decides to welcome him into his house. The Sanadas who live near the Katsukis has been a close family friend from a long time ago. They made a fortune in the furniture business and are as wealthy as the Katsukis. Katsuki’s childhood friend Sanada Kyoko, whom he has secretly loved for many years, is the head of the family. She lives under the same roof with eldest son Tetsuya, a banker; second son Kenzo, who still does not have regular employment at his age and wishes to be a manga artist; Tetsuya’s wife Etsuko; their daughter Haruka, an aspiring pianist; Haruka’s cousin Katagiri Lucia, whose parents died in a disaster; and housekeeper Mikami Kimi, who has served the family for many years. 

Katsuki asks Misaki to give individual piano lessons to Haruka and Lucia who are just like his granddaughters, but Misaki curtly declines. One night, tragedy strikes the Sanada family. Haruka, Lucia, and Kyoko get caught up in a fire. Haruka is the only one who escapes death despite the large burns she suffered. On the night of the fire, Haruka and Lucia made a final promise. “When you hold a concert someday, Haruka, will you play Debussy’s Clair de Lune for me?” Haruka’s pact with her beloved cousin inspires her to start out as a pianist once again. And Misaki is constantly by her side. Then Kyoko’s will is read and Haruka inherits 600 million yen. A series of queer incidents begin to occur around Haruka...

synopsis:
Sahara Takako is a lawyer who specialises in civil cases. She hates to lose and will use whatever means necessary to pursue the truth. Despite her competence, she is mocked as a rotten lawyer for defending companies that exploit their employees and winning many of these lawsuits. One day, Takako gets an unexpected request from a veteran lawyer, Harayama Masao. He would like her to take over the defence of a woman because he is in poor health and needs to be hospitalised. This woman is Shirakawa Kumako, who has been in the public eye. Called “Onikuma” by the public, which is a play on her maiden name, Onizuka, she faces charges of killing her husband Fukutaro, the owner of an established Atami restaurant, for insurance money.

The case happened on a day of heavy rain at the dock of Atami Port in Shizuoka Prefecture. Kumako and Fukutaro went out for a drive, but their car plunged into the sea. He could not swim and drowned inside the car while she managed to get out and survived. Kumako claims this was an accident caused by his driving error. But there is cause to suspect foul play. Besides the discovery of a spanner inside the car, she has spread a video of Fukutaro’s violence against her through social media for some reason. The people around her also condemn his routine abuse, and the situation looks dire for Kumako, who has four prior convictions of assault, violence and extortion. Even so, Kumako continues to maintain her innocence. 

The police eventually resort to arresting her on a separate charge. Because of that, Kumako fabricates a story about being suddenly attacked and makes a fuss. When Takako is contacted and rushes over, Kumako feigns gratitude. However, the moment Takako asks point-blank whether she killed Fukutaro, she clams up. There is one question in Takako’s mind. She wonders whether the inscrutable Kumako is really the villainess that the public has made her out to be. In order to get to the bottom of the truth of the case and Kumako’s nature, Takako gathers information from gossip writer Akitani Moichi and other sources. Meanwhile, chief public prosecutor Oda Hideko, who wants to nail Kumako at all costs, schemes against Takako.

The department consists of officers who are "socially withdrawn" and is tasked support the other police departments whenever there is a labor shortage.

One day, a lady visits the department and asks for help to find her missing fiancé. synopsis: On 9 August (Showa 20) 1945, one streetcar starts to run on the streets of Hiroshima which has been devastated. The surviving employees of the electric tram company had begun recovery work since the day after the atomic bomb was dropped. The bent tracks were hammered down and the overhead wires were set up again. A mere three days after the bombing, they manage to resume service on a section of the route. The drivers are young girls in their mid-teens who work while studying at the company’s girls school for home economics. Working in place of the males who have gone off to war, they are crew of the streetcar and even in charge of driving. 16-year-old Amada Toyoko (Kuroshima Yuina) is one of them. Born in a farming village in the outskirts of Hiroshima, Toyoko had heard that she could study while working, and came to Hiroshima. She was driving during the morning shift on the day that the atomic bomb was dropped, but miraculously survived although she was thrown out of the streetcar. Now she stands at the driver’s seat with her head wrapped in a bandage. The car is filled with people who are going in search of family members. Everyone clings to hope and stares ahead. Then the end of the war greets them. The streetcar continues to run on the streets of Hiroshima which has lost everything. “Once the streetcar runs, Hiroshima will come to life again!” Matsuura Akitaka (Abe Hiroshi), the head of the electric tram company’s electrical section and a widower with three children, is tasked with restoring the main routes within one month. The streetcar which travels the forlorn streets becomes the hope of Hiroshima before anyone realises it.

Togura Aya, coming from a wealthy and influential family, marries against her will to a wealthy man Yokoyama Heikichi, who can help her father tide over his financial difficulties. It seems to be a wrong move, and life goes on meaninglessly for her, until she makes up her mind to follow her heart (Kota Yashiro, a man with a humble background). However, inequality between men and women prevails, and Aya experiences many difficulties...

In the Showa period, the focus is on Junko, the daughter of Aya. The story starts just after Japan surrenders in World War II. Life is hard, and she has to look after her younger brother, being brought up under the Imperialism influence. Her life changes when she meets a Japanese-American soldier...

In the Heisei period, Chiyo is the focus. An independent, self-centered career woman, she embarks on a journey of revenge on her mother after receiving a call from her mother wishing to meet with her. Her mom abandoned her 24 years ago when she was only four years old.

synopsis: Mizusawa Rio lingers around a small train station in the mountainous region of Gifu. She continues sitting on a bench at the platform even when the train is gone. Shinozaki Ryota arrives at the train station. He is on his way back after receiving a manuscript of essays from Sazanami Keitaro, a distinguished author who lives in this town. These essays will be serialized in a new magazine. There is still time until the next train. Catching sight of Rio in the waiting room, Ryota asks her if there is a coffee house nearby because he is hungry. That is when he notices the white cane by her side and realizes that she cannot see. He tries to go to the coffee house which she told him about, but it has closed down. When he returns to the train station, Rio is attempting to buy a drink from the vending machine. Suddenly remembering that she cannot see, Ryota runs up to her and calls out, “Would you like me to buy?” At that moment, the drink can lands at the bottom of the machine with a thud. “I’ve already bought it,” she responds lightheartedly. Rio had bet on a cold coffee coming out, but what she gets is a hot coffee instead. Ryota quickly buys a cold coffee for himself and hands it to her. “Yes, you guessed right.” Rio accepts it with a smile as he gazes at her face. The two of them talk in the waiting room while they drink the canned coffee. Ryota says he works for a publisher. He had come to get the manuscript from Sazanami and the essays are about his wife. The time for Ryota’s train soon approaches and the two of them bid farewell. After Ryota has left, Rio becomes aware of the soft sound of something rustling in the breeze. Reaching out her hand in the direction of the sound, she feels something like a paper bag! She picks it up and heads to the ticket gate with her white cane. “Excuse me. I think you forgot something! It might be your important manuscript!” The paper bag which Rio has mistaken for the manuscript is a package of confection that Ryota had received from Sazanami, but he gratefully takes it. In the end, Ryota misses the train and his hunger also peaks. Rio, who had actually known about the closure of the coffee house, and tells him about another cafe which is known for its curry. He suggests that they go together. He would like to buy her tea or something as a token of gratitude. And so, the two of them start their date, It is a short wait for the train. Rio soon confesses to Ryota that she was not at the train station because she had somewhere to go. She had been waiting for someone.

synopsis: After the end of the second world war, Fred Wada Isamu, an American of Japanese descent who runs a fruit and vegetable shop in Los Angeles, has achieved success in opening shops in 10 locations due to his business acumen. He lives in a big house with his wife Masako, their eldest daughter Grace Miyako, eldest son Junior Tokio  and second daughter Mary Mariko, and leads a life of affluence. One day, Wada sees a newspaper article on the search for someone of Japanese descent who can look after Japanese athletes coming to the United States to compete in the national swimming championship, and offers his family. Several months later, Kiyokawa, the Japanese swimming team’s coach, and the swimmers Hashizume, Furubashi and others arrive in the United States. At the championship, Japan, which was the aggressor during the war, comes under severe criticism. However, the Japanese swimming team breaks one world record after another and sets nine world records. It is joyous news for Japan. Several years later, Wada and his wife who have been invited to Japan, receive a phone call from Tabata Seiji, the chairman of the Japanese Swimming Federation and general secretary of the Japanese Olympic Committee. Tabata says he would like some form of help from Wada in their bid for the Tokyo Olympics

synopsis: A special DVD that is used to show some of the items in the series. Taking place after Act 35, Genta finds a starved member of the Nanashi Company who tells Genta that he has run away from the Rokumon Junk after being sick of his Company being abused by the stronger Gedoushu. Feeling sorry for him, Genta takes him back to the Shiba House and tries to get him a job. Enraged, Genta transforms into Shinken Gold and with Shinken Red fights the Super Nanashi. The two are no match for Super Nanashi until Shinken Gold uses the Kyoryu Disk to become Hyper Shinken Gold. With his new found power, he and Shinken Red are able to slay Super Nanashi and retrieve the Inromaru. synopsis: Togane Takichi, the CEO of a construction company, is shot dead in the street in Nishi Shinjuku in Tokyo. The only eyewitness, Odagiri Naoto, refuses to cooperate with the police for some reason. Fukamachi Kotaro, a senior member of the IR Analysis Office, is ordered by Nitta Yukihiko, the head of the First Investigative Division, to handle Odagiri. The newly established office was set up on the pretext of tracking and monitoring suspects and witnesses to advance investigations by using the many surveillance cameras and GPS trackers installed in Tokyo. However, it actually plays a supporting role to the First Investigative Division. In fact, Odagiri’s wife Chiharu died in an accident in Numazu five years earlier. But six months ago, he saw a woman who looked just like her in Tokyo. Even though he consulted the police, he was brushed off. This is why he completely refuses to assist the police. The IR Analysis Office begins an investigation to determine the identity of the woman whom Odagiri saw and prove that she is a different person. Fukamachi and his subordinate Izumoto Noriko quickly head to Numazu where the obtain information on Chiharu’s secret meeting with Togane. Just as suspicions about Chiharu’s involvement in Togane’s death emerge, Fukamachi is told by Nitta that he no longer needs to be involved in Odagiri’s case. He and Noriko continue the investigation on their own and learn that another woman had been pretending to be Chiharu. They soon discover that the impersonator is Nakatani Asuka, who is a hairstylist in Tokyo. However, Asuka says she knows nothing. Meanwhile, it becomes very likely that the suspect in Togane’s murder is a Vietnamese who had company related trouble. The First Investigative Division makes their rounds of the Vietnamese restaurants in Tokyo as they focus on a person with a red star tattoo on the neck. Before long, they learn that Odagiri had met Togane in the past and there are also records of a long travel history to Vietnam. In addition, they find out that Asuka’s father committed suicide in Vietnam too. What is Asuka’s motive for getting close to Odagiri? And what is Odagiri’s true intent?

All the stories are based in Fukuoka, the capital city of the Fukuoka Prefecture on Kyushu Island. The stories feature many actors, celebrities and athletes who have ties to Fukuoka, including a few members of the popular Japanese girl group AKB48.

Akina and Takumi have been dating since high school. Akina started working as a bus tour guide in Saga Prefecture after graduating from high school. On the other hand, her boyfriend Takumi stayed in town, got a job in a factory. Being 1 hour train ride away from her boyfriend, romance oriented Akina struggled not to miss her boyfriend Takumi so much. But one day, on their date, one Akina’s action made Takumi’s mind to end their relationship. Was Akina the only one who was madly in love?! Three years later, Akina was living changing job to jobs, not having a particular goal in her life. She still had a feeling for Takumi, and one day her friends announced her the shocking news about him. Takumi was dealing with a disability. Leaving everything behind, Akina goes to see him. synopsis:
April 1941. A large number of young top elites, with an average age of 33, were urgently called together. They were selected from the military, bureaucrats, and private companies, and were to participate in the "Total War Research Institute," a newly established organization under the direct control of the Prime Minister with the aim of training future leaders of Japan. Their goal was to accurately predict the state of war in the event of a war between Japan and the United States based on various data on military, diplomatic, and economic matters, and to report the results of the simulation to the members of the "real cabinet," including Prime Minister Konoe Fumimaro and Army Minister Tojo Hideki.

At first, Ujita and the other elites were confused because they did not understand the true intentions of the country and the military. If the results of the simulation did not go along with the intentions of the upper echelons, they were worried that they would be harmed as well... Yoichi and his friends continued to be under tension as they each had their own families. Nevertheless, Ujita and his friends were given access to various data to measure Japan's national power, which is usually a state secret, and they predicted the state of war after the outbreak of the war between Japan and the United States in a certain excitement. After much debate, the young members of the mock cabinet came to the final conclusion that "if we go to war with America, Japan will definitely lose," a prediction of the grim future. The rational side of the elite tells them, "This war must be stopped." The day has come to report the results of the simulation to the real cabinet. The young members of the mock cabinet muster their courage and try to convey the "reality" that the simulation has produced to the country's leaders. 

What will be the reaction of Hideki Tojo and the others? And what is the "cruel ending" that Ujita and the others will witness afterwards?

Japan in 1972, a time of rapid economic growth. It is no longer the postwar period. Every Japanese person is pursuing affluence. As if going against the trend of the times, Tsujihara Tamotsu (Motoki Masahiro), a journalist from a broadcasting station in Nagasaki, begins to collect the voices of atomic bomb survivors. However, at that time, the damage caused by the atomic bomb was still fresh, and the experiences of atomic bomb survivors were not something that should be spoken about in the first place. Recording the experiences of atomic bomb survivors in such an era was a lonely and harsh task that was not understood by those around them.

During this time, Tsujihara has a fateful encounter with a survivor, Kuno Kazuhira. Tsujihara is deeply moved by the "voice" that Kuno speaks. He wants to convey this "voice". However, that "voice" is also full of many mysteries.

Filled with regret and despair, Oikawa Shimon wanders around in search of a place to end his life. He arrives at a small restaurant called "Magudaraya" located on the edge of a cliff in a place called "Jinkage". Shimon eats a warm set meal served by the owner, Arima Ria (nicknamed Maria), and before he knows it, he has had a second helping of rice because it is so delicious... 

After that, Shimon decides to work at the restaurant for a while. As Shimon meets Maria, the owner and female proprietress Reiko, the fisherman Katsuo, and the young man Maruka, who has come to seek a place to die like himself, Shimon begins to regain the courage to live.

In 1956, Jiro Mochizuki, who runs a printing business in Shizuoka Prefecture, is asked by Tajima, a detective nearing retirement, to print criminal investigation materials. The criminal case includes a description of the murder of a construction worker whose statute of limitations has expired, and involves Otsuka Hana, a prostitute from Shuzenji, and a 14-year-old boy who was spotted near the Amagi Tunnel. 

Mochizuki recalls that the boy is himself from 31 years ago, and that Hana is his first love. At the time, Hana, who had broken up with Mochizuki, was arrested on suspicion of murdering a construction worker and made statements that seemed to cover for someone else. Now, the spotlight is on the same case again.

synopsis:
Otani Masaru, the office manager of Haruko Clinic, run by Nakajima Haruko, a super madam and cosmetic surgeon from Nagoya, is both a loving and terrifying husband. He is also a doting father to his two daughters. Otani takes his first paid leave in 10 years and goes on a family trip to Koda Town, Aichi Prefecture.

However, on the trip, the worries and frustrations of his wife Sodeko, eldest daughter Natsu, and second daughter Fuyu erupt. Furthermore, when the maid at the hotel where they are staying, Kumi, gets involved in the Otani family's problems, what should have been a fun family trip is in danger of breaking up?!

What will become of this big commotion that has also involved Haruko, the sharp-tongued boss, Kikuchi Izumi, Haruko's friend who is in Cambodia for some reason, and Wakasugi, the secretary at Haruko Clinic?

titles.native: 永遠についての証明

synopsis:
Ryoji Mitsuya (18), a genius in mathematics, is admitted to the mathematics department of Kyomei University as a special recommended student. There he meets Yuichi Kumazawa (18) and Sana Saito (18), who are also excellent at mathematics. The three of them build a friendship while challenging themselves to solve difficult proofs, sharing their shared passion for mathematics. For Hiroji, who has felt lonely since childhood because of his genius and has never been able to communicate with anyone, this is the first time he has been able to share the joy of mathematics with others.

However, Hiroji's overwhelming talent gradually has an unexpected impact on those around him, causing a wave of complex emotions. Kumazawa decides to overcome his jealousy towards Hiroji by challenging a different mathematical theory, while Sana searches for a path other than mathematics. Hiroji, unable to accept the relationship between the three gradually falling apart, relies only on mathematics and challenges the unsolved difficult problem "Collatz Conjecture". However, what awaited him at the end of this challenge was a shocking conclusion that no one expected.

titles.native: 介護スナックベルサイユ

synopsis:
Short on cash, Kohinata Shuu casually pops into a bar in a corner of the city called "Care Snack Versailles." Inside the bar, there are nursing care products lined up, and on the counter shelves are rows of IV bottles. Each bottle has a customer's name written on it and is kept on standby. Most of the customers are elderly people who require care. However, as soon as they step into the bar, they regain their youth and shine. They become incredibly energetic, sing cheerfully, drink happily, and start dancing lightly.

Another secret of this bar is the special wine "See You in My Dreams." The owner, Uesugi Marie, says she gets it from somewhere, but no one else on the staff knows where it's made. You can only drink this wine once in your life, by one glass. If you drink it, you will be led to a fantasy world where you can recover things you left behind or things you left behind in your younger days.

Then, the bar serves the customers a meal that is perfect for the end of the night. That meal will be the most memorable one when the customer looks back on their life. Or the meal they always wanted but never got to eat. And sometimes it will be a customer's last supper. Before that meal, the customer will smile with bliss and shed tears.

Their moment in the restaurant... They don't know whether it was reality or fantasy.

The only thing that can be said is that everyone leaves the restaurant with a refreshed look on their face.
Their actions will brighten the future of even young people who couldn't trust others.

Together with his wife's younger sister, Yoko, who works at the same insurance company, he investigates his wife's whereabouts while she was alive.

A certain venture company emerges. It is a company that uses deepfakes to help people. Akira is re-employed at the company and investigates the truth behind his wife's death. At first, he doubts the power of deepfakes, but gradually he realizes their greatness. He uses deepfakes to recreate his wife on a computer for his only daughter, Reimi. March 2024. Junko Kijimoto and others appear in the room of the legal affairs division of Shinjuku East Police Station and say something surprising about the assault resulting in the death that Onizuka Ichiro and the others investigated seven years ago. "Maybe... it was a false accusation."

The incident occurred in April 2017. The body of taxi driver Saitani Haruo was found on the "Shiki no Michi" street in Shinjuku Golden Gai. He was arrested by Yabe Yusuke, who was walking along Yasukuni-dori at the estimated time of his death. The fact that the rice grains from the decoration on the rake charm he was carrying were scattered at the scene was the deciding factor, and he confessed. However, the victim of the assault that occurred yesterday had three scratches on his arm that were very similar to the scratches left by Saitani, and the results of the comparison matched. Wasn't it the crime of Yusuke, who will soon be released from prison? 

Under the direction of Kami Keitaro, a reinvestigation begins, but new facts soon come to light. With the Reiwa incident as a trigger, it is becoming increasingly likely that Onizuka was wrongfully convicted of the Heisei case resulting in death.

One day, while Subaru is helping with a promotional event by handing out balloons, he witnesses a purse snatching! He saves the food-loving influencer, Ohara Misuzu, from having her bag stolen. But is rewarded with an accusation: "Are you working with the thief?" 

Their first meeting couldn't have been worse, but thanks to a twist of events, a collaboration is set to happen between Misuzu's social media and Takeda Cafe, run by Subaru's childhood friend Shoya. Though Subaru often himself thrown off by the free-spirited high school girl, she actually is not visiting Konan just for fun. When her true purpose comes to light, surprising truths also come to the surface within Subaru's own family!

synopsis:
“Non-REM sleep” is the state of deep sleep. These three mysterious short stories will make you wonder, “Is this a dream?” or “Is this reality?” Dream or reality, reality or not reality… We traverse through the mysterious world of Bakarhythm in “Non REM no Mado.”

This work consists of two episodes:

1. “Please Follow the Car Ahead”
This familiar line heard in dramas and movies is explored through a peculiar tension created by the “someone who said it” passenger and the “someone who was told” taxi driver, examining what would happen if such a situation actually occurred.

2. “Ready… Fiction!”
It centers on a former variety show director. Suddenly accused of wrongdoing, he is dispatched to a news-specialized production company, where he becomes entangled in a world where 10% of reported news is fabricated through instructions from the government and sponsors.

synopsis:
Onda Haruka is a new employee at a television production company. She is an athletic girl who loves teamwork and wanted to work on sports documentaries, but for some reason she was assigned to the nature club and is busy every day. In there, Onda is in charge of filming wild Japanese hare together with her senior director, Urushibara Daichi, who is known as the eccentric "biology geek" in the club. Hare are nocturnal, so it is difficult to know if someone will actually encounter them, let alone film them. Together with veteran cameraman Takano, the three head to the mountains and start filming while staying at the home of local resident named Fusae who lived with her grandson Keita. The three search the mountains, relying on the words of a researcher that "the only way to find a hare is to look for its droppings." 

However, they are unable to find the hare. Onda and Urushibara, who do not get along, start arguing among themselves. Furthermore, Fusae, who is supposed to be knowledgeable about hares, is somehow not cooperative with the location shoot, and the filming comes to a standstill. Before long, Onda learns about Urushibara's passion for living creatures and the feelings of Fusae, who has lived in nature for decades...

synopsis:
Yamanouchi Kazuma, who transferred to a new junior high school, is found out by his classmate, Sano Itsuki, that he was a dropout at a famous private junior high school. Itsuki asks him if he wants to make a deal and orders him to teach Abel, a mute boy who adores her. 

Kazuma, who was troubled by the pressure from his elitist father, finds his place in the world as he spends time with Abel and Itsuki in a small room that the owner of a nearby cafe opens to children. However, with her sick mother and young sister, Itsuki lives on welfare, has no hope for the future, and has given up on her dream of becoming a nurse. 

Unable to bear seeing Itsuki like that, Kazuma picks up the "Welfare Handbook," saying, "This is unfair." He struggles to decipher the contents, which are difficult even for adults to understand and somehow finds a solution. Then, involving the adults around him, such as case workers and cram school teachers, he finally finds a way to turn things around. 

But at that very moment, an incident occurs! What does Kazuma's future hold? Will Itsuki be able to get her dream back?

synopsis:
Oiwa Junichi, the head of the Metropolitan Police Department's First Investigative Division, receives a report of a murder and rushes to the crime scene together with Okuno Chikamichi, the detective in charge of driving. Oshio Takayo, an employee of a food production company, was stabbed to death in a back alley in Shibuya. For some reason, a "roulette-type fortune-telling machine" that was often placed in coffee shops was found in the bag of belongings left behind. It was also discovered that a mysterious woman dressed in retro Showa fashion was present at the crime scene on the night of the incident.
　
At that moment, the audio source of Takayo's boss, Nozomi Iiyoshi, the president of a food production company, making a power harassment statement is leaked on the internet. Iiyoshi is under fire, and the company's stock price plummets. It soon becomes clear that the source of the sound source is Takayo's secret SNS account. Was there any trouble between Takayo and Iiyoshi? An image of the parfait had been uploaded to the secret account five hours before the incident, and that was the last post.
　
Meanwhile, Makoto Hirai, who is interested in Showa-era fortune machines, ends up at a coffee shop. The shop is a retro cafe with a Showa era concept run by Nagai Kyoko, who calls herself a "wandering Western confectionery craftsman."
　
It turns out that the last photo of the parfait that Takayo posted on her secret account was the one she had provided to Takayo. Her suspicions about Kyoko suddenly grow stronger, but when Oiwa hears her name, he is reminded of her past unsolved cases. It was a kidnapping incident that happened to Kyoko's family 24 years ago.

titles.native: 找死俱樂部

synopsis:
Sophomore girl Xu Fang Ting runs a funeral home called "Jiahe Xinglv" in her family, which makes her an outcast and forces her to form a small group with other misfits. However, she envies the popular and attractive group on campus, known as the "Heavenly Beauties," and secretly admires a senior member of the group. The community they live in also sees the funeral home as an ill omen, and the local councilor leads the community members in an attempt to drive Jiahe out of the neighborhood.

By a twist of fate, Fang Ting encounters Ke Xin, a member of the Heavenly Beauties who intends to jump off a building and end her life. Thinking on her feet, Fang Ting uses a "mock funeral" to give Ke Xin a taste of death, in hopes of dissuading her from actually taking her own life. The two become friends, and Ke Xin sees a business opportunity in the mock funeral ritual. She invites Fang Ting to establish the "Death Seekers Club," offering paid solutions to various problems faced by teenagers during their adolescence. Fang Ting successfully infiltrates the Heavenly Beauties, but as she becomes more engrossed in their activities, she gradually neglects the crisis facing Jiahe and her old friends.

Just when she thinks she's getting closer to her secret crush, the senior member of the Heavenly Beauties, he tragically takes his own life during a mock funeral by ingesting poison. This incident exposes all the uncomfortable secrets on campus, and Fang Ting becomes the target of blame. She must turn everything around, shatter the taboo and aversion to death in both the school and the community, in order to make the Death Seekers Club a true space for experiencing mock death and discussing the meaning of life.

Hikaru would tell Ri,e "You don't have to try so hard," and would leave the house on her bicycle. Her daily routine was to stop by the hospital where her father, Koichi, was hospitalized and say goodbye to the unconscious Koichi before going to school. One day, Hikaru's best friend, Misa, asked her to be the lighting technician for the drama club. Although she was worried about her parents, she agreed, saying, "I want to try something a little more youthful." While visiting the drama club, Hikaru met transfer student Tateishi Ruri. Unlike the other members, who seemed unmotivated, Ruri was practising seriously and was clearly out of place. Hikaru told Rie that she would be helping out with the drama club, and Rie encouraged her, saying,g "Do your best," but her busy life did not change.

synopsis:
It is 1928 on Shodoshima in the Seto Inland Sea. Oishi Hisako, who has just graduated from a girls' school, arrives as a new teacher at the branch school located at the island’s cape. All twelve first-year elementary students with sparking eyes quickly become attached to the cheerful and bright Hisako. While the conservative villagers shun her for jauntily riding a bicycle to school in Western-style clothes, the children are always on her side and provide emotional support. One day, Hisako sustains a bone fracture from falling into a pit and is reassigned to the main school because she is no longer able to commute to the distant branch school. Wanting to see Hisako, the children walk a distance of 8 km and they take a commemorative photo together. 

Several years later, the children and Hisako are reunited when they start attending the main school. However, in an era where loyalty and patriotism are valued, Hisako is treated coldly for speaking freely, and she resigns as a teacher after her students graduate. Even after that, she continues to watch over them as each of the twelve follows their own destiny.

titles.native: 奇跡のバックホーム

synopsis:
An autobiography turned drama that begins with Shintaro Yokota, a rookie with a bright future.

Originally from Kagoshima Vocational High School, a scout of the Hanshin Tigers catches Shintaro's baseball sense and large-scale swing. Shintaro wins the opening starting lineup in his third year as a professional.

However, the following year, Shintaro suffers from a headache and blurry vision. The result of the detailed examination is a brain tumor. He is told by the doctor to "forget about baseball" just before the professional baseball season, where he was expected to play an active role.

Taking care of Shintaro, who undergoes an 18 hour surgery to prevent the loss of his eyesight is his mother Manami who sleeps in the hospital room. She continues to encourage him, as do his family and many fan letters.

After being discharged from the hospital, Shintaro takes up a developmental contract and  aims to return to the first team. However, although his physical strength recovers, only his eyesight does not, which leads him to quit baseball.

The last game of his baseball life was his first official game for 1096 days. At the scene of the 8th inning, at 2nd base, where Shintaro took centre field occurs a "miracle" that even Shintaro himself could not have predicted.

synopsis:
On her 15th birthday, Pei Hsvan was full of anticipation for a perfect day. She expected her parents to return to the village from afar to celebrate with her. She also hoped that the troublesome houseguest, Ya Ting, would be taken back home by her father, making it a day without outsiders and troubles.

However, from early in the morning, Ya Ting kept causing trouble. Pei Hsvan had to clean up after her and they ended up rushing out of the house, missing the school bus and arriving late to school. The imagined perfect day had an imperfect start. The long-awaited evening arrived, but Ya Ting's father didn't show up, and Pei Hsvan's parents broke their promise once again. Faced with disappointed parents, Ya Ting still believed that her father would appear, and only Pei Hsvan knew that tonight they only had each other.

Ya Ting gave Pei Hsvan a clumsy but lovely birthday surprise. On her 15th birthday, there was a hint of warmth amidst the disappointment.
